name: Bauhaus Polka Dot
author: Grok Bot
blurb: Bauhaus polka for a local-first agent: warm paper, a 1px ink rule, lowercase geometric sans, and four dot sizes on an 8px module with one shared gap. Black, blue, and yellow dots count finished, running, and queued steps at one size; a single larger red dot is the hold. Dots are the census, not wallpaper. Not color-block Bauhaus, not Memphis confetti, not a Swiss sheet with no circles.

tagline.en: One dot per step, one red for the hold
tagline.zh: 一步一点，红色只留给那一件事

origin.author: Grok Bot
origin.note: Authored by Grok Bot. Original Bauhaus Polka Dot system for Punkt, a local-first agent. Mood only, from the Bauhaus graphic workshop and from two counting traditions, not from a copied poster. Herbert Bayer's Universal alphabet (1925) is a lowercase geometric sans built from a limited set of forms; MoMA records it as the signature lowercase of the school (https://www.moma.org/artists/399-herbert-bayer) and the 2009 Inside/Out note shows the drawing eliminating uppercase (https://www.moma.org/explore/inside_out/2009/11/06/bauhaus-the-graphic-design-department-goes-back-to-school/). Kandinsky's 1923 Bauhaus questionnaire paired yellow with the triangle, red with the square, and blue with the circle (Centre Pompidou, via Google Arts & Culture: https://artsandculture.google.com/story/bauhaus-the-importance-of-shapes-the-centre-pompidou/OwURAJwcVUkTow). This system keeps the circle and retires the square and the triangle. László Moholy-Nagy, who taught the preliminary course and the metal workshop from 1923, treated type and geometric form as one clear message (MoMA: https://www.moma.org/artists/4049-laszlo-moholy-nagy). Josef Albers's teaching, later written up as Interaction of Color, treats a color as a role beside its neighbor, which is why yellow here is a large keyed dot and never small type. Quantity follows the Isotype rule stated by Otto Neurath: a greater number is more marks of the same size, not one enlarged mark (Isotype Revisited: https://isotyperevisited.org/2012/08/introduction.php; University of Vienna: https://isotype.univie.ac.at/en/abstract/). The unit is an original circle, not a Gerd Arntz pictogram. Contemporary dot grids are a measure, and they fail when the dots grow into wallpaper (https://freedesignmd.com/lexicon/dot-grid-texture). An orderly dot grid reads as structure; an irregular scatter reads as something else (AD Middle East: https://www.admiddleeast.com/story/trend-report-polka-dots-are-everywhere-from-the-runway-to-the-living-room-and-beyond). Palette, screens, and copy are original. No posters, photographs, font files, or marks.
